summary: This sermon explores peace as the third fruit of the Spirit in a series on Galatians 5:22. The preacher contrasts worldly peace—which depends on controlling favorable circumstances—with the peace Jesus offers, which transcends circumstances regardless of external conditions. Through John 14 and Philippians 4, he argues that Christ's peace is accessed not by managing life perfectly but through prayer, gratitude, and focusing on God's goodness.
key_points: The world is experiencing an unprecedented crisis of peace and mental health
Worldly peace requires favorable circumstances we cannot control
Jesus offers a peace that transcends circumstances, not just copes with them
This peace is accessed through prayer, thanksgiving, and meditating on what is good
The story of Horatio Spafford illustrates peace in the midst of tragedy
big_idea: Jesus offers a peace that transcends all circumstances and understanding, accessed through dwelling with the Holy Spirit via prayer, gratitude, and focusing on God's goodness rather than life's troubles.
title: NO Jesus, NO Peace.
